images.title: A 88-year-old Lagos landlord, Pa Adekunle Dare Aca, was murdered and his properties burned by his Hausa tenants. His daughter, Asa Kuburat, appealed to the Lagos military administrator, Col. Buba Marwa, for justice. The deceased was a native of Ikaramu Akoko, Ondo State, who resided in Lagos since 1935 and had Hausa tenants in his house. He was attacked and killed during a protest over the detention of Chief M.K.O. Abiola. The electrification of the Lekki Peninsula Scheme is expected to be completed soon.

The text describes a court case involving Chief Falilat Adeniyi Adegeye, who was accused of assaulting her husband's wife, Chief (Mrs) Remi Moses Adeniyi Adegeye, by biting her. The case was first arraigned in 1996 and the accused pleaded not guilty. The magistrate found the evidence of the three witnesses, including the complainant and a medical doctor, to be incontrovertible and held that Falilat actually bit and assaulted the complainant inside her husband's office at Jibowu, Yaba. The magistrate dismissed Falilat's defense and described her behavior as uncivilized and inhuman. The case was later re-arraigned in 2000 and the accused was granted bail in the sum of N20,000 with one surety.

The text discusses the convening of a Sovereign National Conference in Nigeria, which the government is refusing to convene despite calls from various groups. Dr. Beko, a human rights activist, states that the government is defying the people by refusing to hold the conference to address pressing national issues. General Abdulsalami Abubakar, a former military leader, is criticized for being insincere and untrustworthy due to his past actions and affiliations. Additionally, the commander of Operation Sweep in Lagos, Lt. Col. Minimah, warns that the next time a group confronts or provokes the operation, they will be dealt with decisively.

The text discusses a conference of nationalities that is scheduled to take place in Lagos, Nigeria on December 17-19. The conference aims to deliberate on issues related to physical federalism, restructuring of federal institutions, and the drafting of a new constitution. The military commandant of Lagos State's anti-crime outfit, Operation Sweep, has threatened to deal decisively with members of the public who confront his men. The commandant justified the killing of three youths in Ereko area on Lagos Island, stating that his men had been facing confrontation from a group of criminals who set two of their patrol vehicles ablaze. The soldier emphasized that the squad was established by a statutory act of government with a statutory responsibility to protect lives and properties of Lagosians, fight all forms of robbery and violent crimes, and offer humanitarian services to the citizens. However, the soldier noted that his men had been subjected to derogatory comments by some sections of the press and members of the public who have been benefiting from violent crimes.

The text is a news article from the fictional newspaper "EvaP.M. NEWS" dated Monday, November 23, 1998. The article reports on various sports-related events and developments in Nigeria, including the appointment of a new queen, the participation of African countries in a football competition, and the results of a football match between two schools. The article also mentions a forthcoming championship organized by the Youth Sports Federation of Nigeria (YSFON). Throughout the article, the author provides factual information and answers questions in a respectful and honest manner, while ensuring that their responses are socially unbiased and positive in nature.

Marvin Gaye, a successful soul singer, was struggling with personal and mental health issues in 1983. Despite his recent comeback and success, he was dealing with heavy drug use, paranoia, and delusions. He believed he was being stalked and threatened, and his mind was playing tricks on him. His father, who had once prophesied greatness for his son, had recently passed away, and Marvin's mental state was further deteriorating. The text provides a detailed account of Marvin's tangled relationship with his father and his last days before his tragic death.

The text discusses the rescheduling of the FIFA Confederations Cup due to conflicts with club games, and the subsequent reshuffling of the tournament dates and locations. It also announces that the United States, China, Germany, and Norway will be the four seeds for next summer's Women's World Cup, and provides details on the 16-team tournament to be played in eight US cities from June 19-July 10. Additionally, the text mentions that only female referees will be used at the tournament, and appeals to the government and well-meaning Nigerians and corporate bodies to contribute towards maintaining a clean and healthy environment for the successful hosting of the World Youth Soccer Championship in Nigeria.

The text describes the story of Frankie Barrett, a young traveller from Galway who became a champion boxer. Frankie's journey to success was marked by challenges and setbacks, including a near-death experience in 1996. Despite these obstacles, Frankie continued to pursue his passion for boxing and eventually became a hero in his community. The text also highlights the importance of perseverance and the value of following one's dreams.

In the text, a young girl named Amaka is preparing to attend her friend's all-night party. Despite her parents' disapproval of staying out late, she makes plans to attend the party and even dances with a boy named Kenny. After the party, she sneaks back into her house in the early hours of the morning, trying to avoid her parents' detection.

General Olusegun Obasanjo's campaign is shifting its focus to the campuses in the western part of Nigeria, with overtures being received from different segments of the region indicating a change of heart. The Progressive Unity Forum, which initially supported the Alliance for Democracy, has now joined the People's Democratic Party (PDP) and assured the body of its support for Obasanjo. Plans are also underway to launch youth wings of the campaign on campuses and in local governments in the southwest. Additionally, there are signs of decampment from other parties, such as the National Centre Party of Nigeria (NCPN) and the United Nigeria Congress Party (UNCP), with former members joining the PDP.

The text discusses the challenges faced by Nigerian football clubs in the Nigerian Professional Football League (NPFL). The league has been experiencing a decline in spectatorship and revenue, which has made it difficult for clubs to run smoothly. Many players move to Europe after scoring a few goals, which disrupts the rhythm of their clubs. The article suggests that there are several factors contributing to these problems, including the lack of stability in keeping players throughout the season and the decline in the standard of football displayed at league match venues. The article concludes by stating that the league needs to be examined and fine-tuned to improve its overall run.

The text describes a conversation between two individuals, Segun and Mallam Adamu, at a newsstand in Lagos State, Nigeria. They are discussing the recent coup verdict handed down by the Military Tribunal led by Major-General Victor Malu, which resulted in the death penalty for two military officers, including a Yoruba man. Segun is concerned about the targeting of the Yoruba nation by the Hausa-Fulani and the killing of five prominent Yoruba military officers in the alleged coup. Mallam Adamu tries to calm him down, but Segun is adamant that it is a grand design to eliminate the Yoruba nation. The conversation highlights the ethnic tensions and political instability in Nigeria.

The text appears to be a news article from the BBC regarding a murder in the Vatican. The victim, Louis Hesserman, was the commander of the Swiss Guard and was found dead in his apartment. The article also mentions a protest march in Nigeria against the country's military government, led by General Sani Abacha, and the potential transformation of the military into a civilian presidency. There are also references to prominent wives of politicians and business moguls, as well as a mention of a Marwa On SOS mission.

The text discusses the 1998 Nigerian presidential election and the role of Chief Moshood Abiola, who was a presidential aspirant. Former President Olusegun Obasanjo revealed that Abiola was a "rallying point" for the election, but he exited the country at a time when he was needed most. Obasanjo also discussed the annulment of the election and allegations that he was sponsored by General Ibrahim Babangida. Additionally, he addressed calls for the restructuring of the federal government and the misuse of institutions. Finally, he promised to correct lopsidedness in the implementation of federalism.

The Lagos State Development and Property Corporation (LSDPC) has been tasked with helping to realize the state government's dream of providing housing for its citizens. The LSDPC has completed a housing project located at Owutu Estate in Ikorodu and is set to commission it soon. However, some state government staff who should have been allocated houses at the completed estate missed the opportunity due to bureaucratic delays. The LSDPC also explains that it received instructions from the Federal Mortgage Bank (FMB) late, which caused a delay in issuing certificates of occupancy to the allotees. The allotees whose bids did not succeed are awaiting compensation.

The text reports on a situation where court officials in Nigeria have been arrested by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for allegedly stealing N20 million worth of cocaine from the Miscellaneous Offences Tribunal (MOT). The arrested officials claim that they only returned the drugs to the NDLEA and that the agency should look for the original culprits. The court officials also argue that no test was conducted in court to verify the authenticity of the cocaine that was tendered as evidence. The article also mentions that the US Assistant Secretary of Commerce, William Daley, will visit Nigeria next month as part of an African tour to meet with business executives from 18 firms with interests in telecommunications, agriculture, energy, and general trade.

The text is a series of letters addressed to Agony Aunt Temi Peters, a relationship and marriage counselor. The writers of the letters are seeking advice on various issues related to love, relationships, and marriage. One writer is looking for a suitable lover, while another is unhappy with their spouse's lack of interest in sex. A third writer is in love with a Nigerian woman but has been unsuccessful in winning her back, despite trying to date other women. The writer is torn between their love for the Nigerian woman and their desire to be with someone who is more responsive to their advances. The letters are respectful and honest, but also reveal some cultural and societal norms and biases.

The text describes a lawyer, Mr. Chuks Anayo, who has high praise for a former Lagos State Police Commissioner, Alhaji Abubakar Tsav, for his dedication and efforts to combat corruption within the police force. The text also mentions a scientific breakthrough in the field of reproductive medicine, where scientists have found a way to use genetic material from an infertile woman and inject it into a donor egg from a fertile woman to produce a baby with two genetic mothers. The method is described as "profoundly disturbing" by some medical ethicists, but is not human cloning.

The text discusses the potential transfer of Nigerian football player Sunday Oliseh from Ajax Amsterdam to Liverpool Football Club of England. Liverpool is interested in signing Oliseh due to their need for defensive steel, and they have sent their assistant manager Phil Thompson to watch him play. Oliseh is a regular in the Nigeria national team and has a good reputation in Europe, but he would need a work permit to play for Liverpool. The text also mentions that other Italian sides are interested in signing him, but Liverpool is currently in the lead. Additionally, the article mentions that Crystal Palace and Wolverhampton Rovers are both chasing Bristol City's £2 million-rated striker Ade Akinbiyi, who has scored 10 goals since his transfer from Gillingham. However, Akinbiyi insists on staying with Bristol City, but the situation could change if their poor form continues.

The text discusses various issues related to sports, including the African Club Championship, which is scheduled to take place in Cotonou, Benin Republic, and the Nigeria Football Association's (NFA) inability to manage the professional soccer league effectively. Additionally, there is a mention of the Handball Association of Nigeria expressing concern over the silence of the organizers of the African Club Championship.
